effect: Cold: frost on the terraces, the harvest suffers.
notes: DRAFT. On this coast the cold north-easterly is the bora. Helps ships sailing south.

effect: Heat from Africa: the fields dry out.
notes: DRAFT. Makes the drought card more likely. Helps ships sailing north.

effect: Moist sea air: good for the crops.
notes: DRAFT. Favonius means 'the favourable one', the spring wind of growth.

effect: Warm and wet: the best growing weather.
notes: DRAFT. The Romans also knew Africus as a stormy wind at sea.

effect: No wind: winnowing stalls and ships wait in harbour.
notes: DRAFT. Threshed grain was tossed in the wind to blow away the chaff; with no wind part of the crop stays unclean. Convoys are delayed one season.
